architecture.summary: The habit-hooks cleanup, parts 1 and 2: #297 is merged into this pull request, so the candidate holds both. Part 1 removes comments that the code does not need, in two passes (a first pass and a stricter pass), in src/, test/, and script/. It changes no code: for each of the 307 changed TypeScript files, the print without comments is the same at the merge base and at HEAD. Comments that main rewrote after the classification stay. The declaration snapshots have no comments (removeComments in tsconfig.api-surface.json), so the 16 touched public modules keep identical declarations. Part 2 changes the habit-hooks configuration only: .habit-hooks/config.toml and .habit-hooks/eslint.config.mjs. The line-count sensor gets a limit of 300 lines instead of 200 and skips test/ and the four WorkOS legal-text bundles, which hold data that a SHA-256 pins. no-unused-vars ignores a using declaration, because its binding exists for its dispose (src/index.ts). The five ESLint import-boundary blocks for src/auth, src/mcp, src/hosted-admin, src/page-fetch, and src/search-pipeline go: #214 removed those folders, so the blocks matched no file. The phase-one/import-context rule still applies the component graph of the rules file to each src file, and the dependency_graph of the PR checker guards the same boundaries at review. The policy flag is set: part 2 relaxes what habit-hooks enforces. The protected policy paths (script/pr-review/** and .habit-hooks/**) and twelve security guarantee files select T1 Team review. No component, dependency edge, public module, declaration, contract, external dependency, composition, build output, or deployment relationship changes, and no behavior of the product or of the PR checker changes. The component registry describes the runtime system only; its prose and all 21 views remain accurate and unchanged.
